text: The Patriots' turnover woes came back to haunt them Thursday night in Chicago, as Caleb Williams and the Bears dispatched New England 30-24 in a matchup that underscored one of Mike Vrabel's core pillars of team identity—ball security—with the Patriots continuing to struggle in that critical area through Week 7. Drake Maye and the Patriots offense had some bright spots, notably Rhamondre Stevenson reaching a career high in receiving yards and quietly approaching 100 carries for the sixth consecutive season, but the defensive performance and overall execution weren't enough to overcome Chicago's attack. The team was also dealing with the absences of starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown due to injury, which certainly didn't help matters on an already difficult Thursday night road trip. With film review now underway and postgame analysis pointing to clear areas for improvement, the overarching takeaway for New England is simple: if this team wants to string together wins, controlling the football and winning the turnover battle has to become non-negotiable going forward.
